events.body:
## Outcome

Turn the existing public catalog, activity, star, and mirror data into useful repository discovery views.

## Implementation

- Add `newest`, `recently-active`, `most-mirrored`, `most-starred`, and alphabetical sort modes to the repository catalog query.
- Reuse bounded catalog queries and aggregates; do not issue one request per repository.
- Add online and integrity-verified filters plus a direct clone action.
- Use owner and repository as a stable tie-break so pagination cannot reorder equal scores.
- Add keyboard, mobile, empty, loading, and error states to the public repository view.

## Acceptance criteria

- Sort results are deterministic across repeated requests.
- Private and unlisted records never enter rankings or aggregate counts.
- Ranking adds no per-repository request fan-out.
- Filters combine correctly and preserve the selected sort.
- Clone actions use the stable Git URL already returned by the catalog.

## Dependencies

None.

## Verification

Cover score ties, privacy filtering, pagination, zero-result filters, degraded mirror data, keyboard navigation, and narrow viewports.

events.body:
## Outcome

Make global public repository discovery searchable, useful, and directly cloneable from the default public entry point.

## Implementation

- Add bounded full-text search plus newest, newly mirrored, time-window trending, recently collaboration-active, most mirrored, most starred, and alphabetical views.
- Add verified-maintainer, online, integrity-verified, and minimum-copy filters.
- Use bounded catalog queries and aggregates with no per-repository request fan-out.
- Use owner and repository identity as stable score tie-breakers so pagination cannot reorder equal results.
- Add the discovery view to the default public route with direct clone actions, keyboard navigation, mobile layout, and complete empty, loading, degraded, and error states.

## Acceptance criteria

- Search and rank results are deterministic across repeated requests and pagination.
- Private and unlisted repositories and social records never enter results or aggregates.
- Trending is time-bounded, documented, and resistant to duplicate events.
- Verified-maintainer state comes from scoped identity proofs rather than a display-name claim.
- Every clone action uses a stable Git URL and reports route availability before starting.

## Dependencies

Uses scoped identities from #447 and availability state from #439 as those contracts land.

## Verification

Cover text relevance, every ranking, score ties, duplicate activity, privacy filtering, proof expiry, combined filters, pagination, zero results, degraded routes, keyboard navigation, and narrow viewports.
